![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/generate/scratch/17592186087655/plots/circle-e2e541fa5c78aa1b89874a058665991e4b40edc4f415121fe3c69ac5de926d70.png)

What is the equation of the circle given above?
question.:question/worked-solution:
The general equation of a circle with radius $r$ centered at the point $(a,b)$ is 

$$
(x-a)^{2}+(y-b)^{2}={r}^{2}.
$$

From the picture, we see that our circle is centered at $C(-2,4)$ and the radius of the circle is $r=9.$ Therefore, the equation of the circle is

$$
\begin{aligned}(x-a)^{2}+(y-b)^{2} & ={r}^{2} \\ (x-(-2))^{2}+(y-4)^{2} & ={9}^{2} \\ (x+2)^{2}+(y-4)^{2} & =81.\end{aligned}
$$
